newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate at 11.509 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate at 11.509 pct.

text.p: - The Philippines' bellwether 91-day treasury bill rate edged up to an average of 11.509 percent from last week's 11.476 percent at the regular Monday auction, the Bureau of Treasury said.
But yields on T-bills of other maturities fell. The 182-day T-bill rate averaged at 11.795 percent, down from last week's 11.846 percent; and the 364-day T-bill was at 12.199 from 12.243 percent.
The auction had 7.897 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which 3.500 billion pesos were awarded.
The 91-day bill was the only one that bucked the downward trend because its rates had already gone too low, traders said.
"People were not chasing rates down," said a foreign bank dealer, adding that it was due for a technical rebound.
Banks would rather invest in six-month and one-year bills, the same dealer said.
The 91-day T-bills had the least number of tenders at 1.067 billion pesos, of which 1.0 billion pesos were accepted.
The one-year bills garnered the most number of bids worth 3.800 billion pesos, of which 1.500 billion pesos were sold.
The 182-day bills had 3.030 billion pesos worth of tenders. Awards of 182-day bills were 1.0 billion pesos worth.
